notes: The app can no longer roll itself back to an older version. A downloaded update that was still staged was handed to the phone with NO check that it was actually newer than what you were running — every other path refused an older version, this one did not. So an old bundle left over from earlier (one downloaded for “install later” and never confirmed, or one from a rollback) could be installed on top of a newer build, and the app quietly went backwards. It now only ever moves forward, and refuses anything older out loud

An update the app refuses is taken away from the phone again. Refusing it in the app changed nothing by itself: the native updater applies whatever is queued on its own, every time you leave the app, so it swapped the bundle in anyway and the app came back on the version it had just rejected — over and over. A refused bundle is now handed back to the updater as the version already running, which makes that a no-op

“It updated and then rolled itself back and now it restarts every few seconds” — that loop is gone. If a version was left pinned in the version picker, the app swapped the page back to that old snapshot on every launch while the installed bundle underneath kept updating: install, swap back, install, forever, always reporting the old version. Installing an update now drops the pin, and when an older pinned page is found sitting over a newer installed bundle the app returns to the newest version once instead of fighting it

A failed update can no longer be retried for ever. The record of “we already tried this bundle” lived only in the app’s web storage, which the phone writes to disk in its own time — so an update that took the app down could lose the record and be tried again on the very next launch: install, die, install, die. The bookkeeping is now a real file in the app’s own folder, written and finished BEFORE the bundle is handed over, so it survives the crash it is recording

Three launches inside a minute now means the app is restarting itself, and no automatic bundle change happens at all while that is true — including the ones the phone-side updater would make on its own. Nothing is lost; Check for updates still installs by hand

Confirming a new bundle no longer depends on one file. The “this bundle is good, keep it” signal came only from the updater script; if that script did not load, a perfectly healthy app went unconfirmed and the phone rolled the update back. The app now reports itself healthy too
